verdict.rationale: Requesty's Fallback Policies are a documented, first-party mechanism that automatically retries a failed request (timeout, rate limit, error) by moving to the next model in a configured chain. That covers automatic handling of transient provider errors. However, the evidence only describes failover to different models. Nothing shows configurable retries against the same provider. Missing for 10: same-model/same-provider retry configuration, retry count and backoff settings, per-error-class retry rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can set automatic retry policies for transient provider errors

citations.quote: Fallback Policies automatically retry your requests with different models if one fails, ensuring your application stays reliable even when individual providers have issues.
If it fails (timeout, rate limit, error, etc.), the router immediately tries the next model in the chain.
